source_refs.title: Two-factor authentication for Apple Account - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Steps to turn on two-factor authentication on iPhone
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; the page gives no minimum iOS version. Most accounts already use two-factor authentication. If the Apple Account was created with two-factor authentication, the protection can't be removed.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: 1. Open the Settings app. 2. Tap your name at the top, then select 'Sign-In & Security.' 3. Turn on 'Turn on two-factor authentication' and complete the prompts that appear. Most accounts already use two-factor authentication, so you may not need to enable it. If your Apple Account was created with two-factor authentication, the protection can't be removed.

source_refs.title: Turn on 2-Step Verification - Computer - Google Account Help
source_refs.applicability: Computer; these steps may not work if the account is managed through work, school, or another group
source_refs.model_visible_text: On a computer: 1. Go to myaccount.google.com. 2. Tap 'Security & sign-in.' 3. Under 'How you sign in to Google,' choose 'Turn on 2-Step Verification.' 4. Complete the prompts that appear. If the account is managed through work, school, or another group, these steps may not work. Contact your administrator.
